title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط الثامن
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape eight
body_ar: "وعنعنة المعاصر محمولة على السماع إلا من مدلس\" إذا كان التلميذ لقي شيخه فحدث عنه بعن فهذا يحمل على السماع في حق غير المدلس أما المدلس فإذا قال عن فلا تحمل على السماع لأن هذا من صيغ التدليس وقد سبق التنبيه على ذلك عند ذكر التدليس، \"وعنعنة المعاصر محمولة على السماع إلا من مدلس، وقيل يشترط ثبوت لقائهما\" قيل لا يكفي مجرد المعاصرة بل لا بد من ثبوت اللقي، فالقول الأول هو قول مسلم رحمه الله فكان يرى أن المعاصرة ولو لم يثبت اللقي كافية، فهي إمكان اللقي، مسلم يشترط إمكان اللقي فقط، وأما البخاري فإنه يشترط ثبوت اللقي، ولا يكتفي بمجرد إمكانه، ولذلك قال: \"وقيل يشترط ثبوت لقائهما ولو مرة وهو المختار\" هذا مذهب البخاري واختياره، وأطلقوا المشافهة في الإجازة المتلفظ بها، الإجازة أنواع كثيرة، منها الإجازة العامة، ومنها الإجازة الخاصة، ومنها الإجازة باللفظ ومنها الإجازة بالكتابة ومنها الإجازة المقترنة بالمناولة، ومنها الإجازة بالإذن بالتحديث، ومنها الإجازة بالمشافهة..
body_en:
"And the ʿanʿanah of a contemporary is carried to hearing, except from one who practises concealment (mudallis)." If the student met his teacher and then narrated from him using ʿan ("from"), this is carried to hearing in the case of one who is not a mudallis. As for the mudallis, if he says ʿan, it is not carried to hearing, because this is among the forms of concealment (tadlīs), and attention has already been drawn to that when concealment was mentioned. "And the ʿanʿanah of a contemporary is carried to hearing, except from a mudallis; and it is said that the establishment of their having met is a condition." It is said that mere contemporaneity does not suffice; rather, the meeting must be established. The first view is the view of Muslim, may God have mercy on him: he held that contemporaneity, even where the meeting is not established, is sufficient — that is, the possibility of a meeting. Muslim stipulates only the possibility of a meeting. As for al-Bukhari, he stipulates the establishment of the meeting, and does not content himself with the mere possibility of it. That is why he said: "And it is said that the establishment of their having met, even once, is a condition, and this is the preferred view." This is al-Bukhari's position and his choice.

And they applied "oral communication" without qualification to the licence uttered aloud. The licence (ijāzah) is of many kinds: the general licence; the specific licence; the licence by utterance; the licence in writing; the licence combined with the handing over [of the book]; the licence by permission to narrate; and the licence by oral communication..

flags.note: PRONOUN REFERENT UNCLEAR. The possessive in ikhtiyāruhu could attach to al-Bukhari, the nearer noun, or to Ibn Hajar, who has just endorsed the view in the words being quoted ('and this is the preferred view'). Reading it of Ibn Hajar makes the better sense — the Sheikh would be saying that the requirement of an established meeting is al-Bukhari's doctrine and is also what the author of the Nukhbah prefers — but that is an inference. Option 2 reproduces the ambiguity of the Arabic rather than resolving it, which is what the style guide requires where the Sheikh has not resolved it himself.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani's Nukhbat al-Fikr, a short manual of hadith terminology. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 628–637 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and even then a gap remains (see the note on the download filenames).

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text is the opening of a lecture and breaks off; the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

'ʿAnʿanah' is a narrator's use of the bare particle ʿan ('from so-and-so') rather than an explicit statement of hearing. It is kept in the Arabic because the whole passage is about that specific form of words; no English equivalent carries it.

'Concealment (tadlīs)' is a narrator's practice of making a chain appear stronger than it is, typically by omitting a weak intermediary; a mudallis is one known for it. 'Concealment' has been preferred to 'deception', which overstates the moral charge the term carries in this literature.

The disagreement between Muslim and al-Bukhari on whether contemporaneity suffices or an actual meeting must be shown is the substance of the passage; both positions are attributed expressly and neither has been collapsed into the other.

'Licence (ijāzah)' is a teacher's authorisation to transmit a text, and 'the handing over' is munāwalah, the physical delivery of the book that may accompany it. The final list breaks off after the seventh kind.
The source runs the passage on the licence directly on from the preceding sentence with a comma. A paragraph break has been inserted in body_en only, where the subject changes; body_ar is as served.
